messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple pods in gpu-pool-7 reporting CUDA OOM while headroom shows ~1.2GB free. Triggered by a high-throughput reranking job. Auto-scaling not triggered (pool at max_count=8). Paging count rising.
ryan (oncall): I'm taking it. Observed 5xxs for customer 'FinCore' on /v1/rerank for the last ~3m.
sophie (cs): FinCore reporting spikes in errors and increased latency, pushing support. They see timeouts and occasional 'server error' bubbled up. ETA on root cause?
ryan (oncall): quick triage: `kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=gpu-pool-7` shows 3 pods in CrashLoopBackOff. `nvidia-smi` on node shows about 2.5GB free but our runtime logs show allocation failures for ~256MB chunks. Suspect fragmentation / reserved-blocks mismatch.
maya (eng-runtime): That pattern rings a bell — allocator complaining even with headroom if reserved-blocks are fragmented or pinned by inactive CUDA contexts. Can you paste the runtime allocator dump (`/debug/alloc_state`)?
ryan (oncall): Pasting excerpt:```
ALLOC_STATE snapshot:
total_gpu=24576MB
reserved_pool=8192MB
cached_mapped=2048MB
active_allocated=16832MB
free_contiguous_max=192MB
fragmentation_ratio=0.42
reserved_blocks: [128MB x 10, 256MB x 8, 512MB x 4]
pending_reservations: 3
failure: allocate 256MB -> no contiguous region
```
ryan (oncall): So headroom metric (free memory) counts non-contiguous fragments and reserved_pool, but allocation requires contiguous segments and some blocks pinned by KV cache.
maya (eng-runtime): Makes sense. Also seeing repeated `cudaGetLastError: out of memory` in container logs. The allocator uses a reserved-block cache to avoid driver churn, but with many short-lived contexts + prefix cache retention we get holes.
alex (eng-sre): Node-level view: kernel OOMs not triggered, no GPU reset. It's allocator-level fail. Paging (host swap) is increasing. Could be that reserved_pool is allocated in small blocks causing lookaside fragmentation.
ryan (oncall): Immediate mitigation options proposed: 1) Evict prefix/KV cache on affected model routes. 2) Temporarily lower reserve_pool per-worker via env `REDWOOD_RESERVED_MB=4096`. 3) Drain/roll pods on gpu-pool-7 so allocator resets. 4) Disable continuous batching for that route. Which to run now?
maya (eng-runtime): Start with 1 and 4 — evict caches and disable continuous batching for FinCore rerank. That should free contiguous ranges quickly without node restarts. If that doesn't recover within 2-3 mins, drain/roll nodes.
sophie (cs): I'll notify FinCore: "We're investigating, rolling mitigations now — short-term: we'll reduce concurrency for rerank and expect errors to drop in ~5m"
ryan (oncall): Running cache-evict API for model-id fincore-rerank v12 -> `POST /internal/cache/evict {"model":"fincore-rerank","scope":"prefix,kv"}`. Also set route flag `continuous_batching=false` for that route.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: route-flag update for fincore-rerank -> success in 12s.
ryan (oncall): Cache-evict returned success. Watching pods.
maya (eng-runtime): I'm tailing allocator metrics. free_contiguous_max jumped from 192MB -> 1.6GB after eviction. Good sign. But kernel-level paging still elevated — some pinned allocations may take time to be reclaimed.
ryan (oncall): Traffic for FinCore reroute policy now throttled down; 5xxs reduced from 42% -> 8% in last 90s.
sophie (cs): FinCore acknowledging lower errors, thanks. They want root cause and a permanent fix.
maya (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: reserved-block allocator keeps a pool of small pre-allocated blocks to speed up allocations. A combination of large-batch rerank requests (many 256MB chunks) plus long-lived KV cache pinned blocks caused fragmentation; the allocator's best-fit search fails even when aggregate free memory > requested size. Also we observed `pending_reservations` caused by concurrent attempts to reserve contiguous space — they queued and then timed out.
alex (eng-sre): For permanent controls: options: A) change allocator behavior to prefer coalescing free blocks on eviction (hotfix), B) increase minimal block size to reduce fragmentation, C) implement proactive defragmentation (evicting cold KV entries when contiguous free falls below threshold), D) enforce stricter per-route max-batch/sequence defaults.
maya (eng-runtime): Short-term patch: flip allocator flag `COALESCE_ON_FREE=true` and increase `RESERVED_MIN_CHUNK=64MB` for affected pool. Rolling config to pool with canary then wider rollout. I can push a hotfix to canary pool in ~30m, but we need an SRE-approved rollout plan.
ryan (oncall): For immediate stability, I've scheduled a rolling restart of the 3 CrashLoopBackOff pods (graceful drain, then restart) while we monitor. Will keep at most one pod restarting at a time.
ryan (oncall): Running `kubectl rollout restart deployment/gpu-pool-7 -n serving --timeout=5m` but doing it pod-by-pod via cordon/drain to avoid capacity hole.
ryan (oncall): Pod 2 restarted, came up healthy. Logs show allocator init then reclaimed caches. Error rate down to 1.5% for FinCore.
maya (eng-runtime): Good. Also noticed one model instance was holding stale CUDA context from a crashed worker preventing coalescing — hot path for patch: ensure context teardown forces `cudaMemTrim` (or our equivalent) on worker exit. I'll add that to the hotfix.
sophie (cs): Customer update sent: "We applied temporary mitigations (cache eviction, reduced batching) — errors are dropping; engineering is doing a deeper fix and will follow up with RCA and timeline."
ryan (oncall): Handoff: I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand to maya for hotfix rollout. Next on-call shift is @alex in ~2h; leaving notes: watch for fragmentation_ratio > 0.3 and free_contiguous_max < 256MB triggers auto-evict.
maya (eng-runtime): I'll prepare two PRs: 1) allocator coalesce-on-free + context-trim on exit, 2) operator-level guardrail to throttle large-batch reranks when contiguous_free < threshold. Will run canary in gpu-pool-3 first.
alex (eng-sre): I'll follow up on runbook: add step to evict KV cache automatically on OOM-with-headroom alerts and ensure autoscaler considers contiguous_free metric before scheduling.
ryan (oncall): Closing incident thread for active mitigation; leaving it open for RCA doc and postmortem activities. Final impact: FinCore saw ~5m of elevated errors, peak 42% 5xx on rerank route, no data loss, no kernel GPU resets. Mitigation: cache eviction, disable continuous batching, rolling restart of affected pods.
sophie (cs): I'll open support ticket and schedule a customer post-incident call tomorrow.
maya (eng-runtime): Adding note: possible follow-up — evaluate switching to `cudaMallocAsync`-friendly allocator pattern or adopt larger quantized allocations to reduce fragmentation.
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and marked 'mitigated' pending RCA updates.
